Lady Frere serial killer

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
We still tend to think of small towns as a more innocent place, How could a murderer flourish in a place where everyone knows you by name, but behind the comfortable façade of small-town South Africa have lurked some very disturbed individuals. Lady Frere or Cacadu in the Eastern Cape is one such rural town where 11 elderly people were brutally murdered in just 10 months … This is a town beset with fear and haplessness… As many the community expects the killer to strike at any given time. Zangqolweni
The gruesome killings started in December Last year where 50 year old Gcobile Fihla was found dead close to his house, he had been stabbed several times on his upper body and his throat was slit… initially the community though this was an isolated incident, but shockingly in February $ elerly women were killed in one night … the method of killing was very similar to the first murder -with the victims being stabbed several times and their throats slit.
Following the killing Spree the community went on a rampage after they found yet another body ( a partially decomposed body of an elderly woman who had been stabbed and had her throat cut.
The community rounded up 7 young people in the community and 4 were burnt to death, while the others were lynched near a forest.
But the killings didn’t stop; on May 3 elderly people were killed – all consistent with the murderers MO, 3 more would die in the following months with the latest being a 71-year-old man.


Further information:
What we know so Far :
• The Modus Operandi is consistent , victims were stabbed on the upper body several times and had their throats slit.
• The murderer targeted elderly who lived alone, or were alone at the time…it would seem they are from the community or had been stalking them for a while.
• According to the little info released by police,stab wounds and slit is consistent with a right handed person.
• No one in the community has taken responsibility for the vigilante killings.
• According to journalist Lulamile Feni, some of the victims were raped.
• There hasn’t been a murder since July.

Treatment visually :
• More than anything the story needs to capture the currently state of Zangqolweni village, this a rural community gripped by fear,people are afraid to leave their houses at night, there is this sense of eeriness just blanketing this community, especially because the killer hasn’t been found.
• Though the community formed vigilante groups, there is fear that the killer is actually one of their own, we need to capture that fear.
• We may need to touch on rural safety in the story – this may fit into out interview with the SAPS ( if they do grant us one). They have been vocal .. so I don’t think we’ll have a problem.
• We will need to do re-enactments to tell the story, this will make it striking.
• I feel like we should have more of dark / True -crime feel to in – in a rural setting ( we will need a really good camera guy.

Script : Zingqolweni Killer

V/O : Opening scene: Its nightfall in the Eastern Cape and many communities are getting ready to turn in for the night but here in this village, it means stacking your weapons and preparing to fight for yo ur life.
V/O :Since December last year, There’s been 11 brutal killings here, earning this remote area the informal title of being “ The village of death”.
-Dip to black-
Link: This Is Zingqolweni, A village in the heart of the Cacadu Municipality in the Eastern Cape, quiet and picturesque, where everyone knows each other, but behind the seemingly comfortable façade of this rural village is a community living in terror.
V/O For Community leader Gcinikhaya Koki, this is a village on the edge.
Upsound Gcinekhaya Koki: People go to bed not knowing who is next.
-Breathing space -
Masa question : when did this start?
Upsound :This started in December 2020, we were summoned somewhere that somebody has been killed, nobody knew who killed him. Things like pangas were used, knives were used I then got up to the phone called the police, and told them this is the situation we find ourselves in, please come out.
-Time line graphics-
V/ O The body was that of 50-year-old Gcobile Fihla, a well-known community member.He was viciously stabbed and his throat was slit. His mother, Nontukunina Mbhenyane recalls the day she received the devastating news.
Upsound: I was waiting for him to come and fetch my SASSA card to withdraw my pension money in town. He usually wakes up and comes to have tea with me .suddenly people came and told me that he has been murdered.
- Breather-
Upsound: I never had any problems with Gcobile, he was good. We never disagreed, never..chat, he would hang around and run errands for me.
Upsound: I buried him myself, he is buried next to the house, close to me.
V/O Mbhenyane and her granddaughter Porcia now live in constant fear.
Upsound: Nontukunina Mbhenyane: You sleep during the day .but you know at night you will be awake and seated.
Unsound Nontukunina Mbhenyane: There is no place to run to, to run from your house. Where will I run to where they cant kill you.
Upsound Nontukunina Mbhenyane: I would rather die here and follow my son, my only heartbreak is this child, Who will I leave her with?

-Breather- [visuals of the village, eerie music ]
V/O Fihla’s brutal murder was just the beginning of the nightmare for this village, in January 2021 the body of 78-year-old Nowezile Mbovane was found, She had also been viciously stabbed.
-Timeline graphics
V/O Still reeling from the two murders, on the 1st of February the community of Zingqolweni woke up to yet another gruesome discovery, shockingly four bodies were found. The victims had been killed on the same night. Bringing the death toll to 6 people
-Timeline graphic of the victims -
Upsound: Gcinikhaya Koki As the community we started getting worried, as to what’s going to happen next, if there are no arrests next because it looks like anyone who has done this is still running around.
V/O Jonguxolo Khuphiso’s mother, 88-year-old Nowezile Khuphiso was one of the unfortunate victims during this horrific night.
Upsound:Jonguxolo Khupiso I called her in the morning the phone rang and then it went to voicemail. I tried again to call her again and it rang, I thought maybe it was too early in the morning and she was sleeping. I thought I should run there, I then ran into the house and I found that the bed was moved from where it usually is, it was in the middle of the house and she had fallen behind the bed, she had been killed and they had stabbed her.

V/O The body of 88-year-old Mthemkane Mpoqane was also discovered at the scene, he had been brutally stabbed and his throat had been slit.
Upsound;Jonguxolo Khuphiso: That scene comes back to me, I see it as I did then. It will take a while to forget it.
V/O Despite forensic evidence being collected at the scene, Khuphiso is frustrated by the lack of progress in the case.
Upsound Jonguxolo Khuphiso: They came and took our statements and took pictures Once we got to the house they found a denim jacket and a wool glove. From February until today with the DNA, haven’t they found anything at all, if they haven’t arrested the people who did this, it means this won’t end.
- Breather – cut to Masa and Fezeka-
V/O Community activist Fezeka Matshawule has been one of the first people to be called to the gruesome murder scenes.
Unsound: Fezeka: number seven, was a man, we think he was killed on the sixth because the body was found on the 13th or 14th and the body was already decomposed.
- Graphic of timeline-
V/O She believes all the murders were committed by the same perpetrator.
Upsound Fezeka: We are dealing with a monster because these people are killed the same way the cut is one, you only get one cut.
Upsound Gerard Labuschagne: For some reason, this person has an issue with people of this particular age category it seems.
V/O Forensic Psychologist Doctor Gerard Labuschagne studied these gruesome killings.
Gerard Labuschagne Upsound: It’s a small town in a rural area, chances are greater that it could be someone from that environment, it doesn’t seem like robbery was the motive, and cutting people’s throats despite what one might see on tv is not a very typical way of killing .its a lot more difficult than stabbing someone. That point to someone for whatever reason has a lot of built-up aggression, but to say towards that individual but who that individual as a group represent…The question is was his first murder in December 2020.
Link Masa: Some residents have since fled whilst others spend their nights huddled together in groups purely for protection. Many of the people here fear the killer or killers may be amongst them and could strike at any time.

-
Upsound Fezeka People are leaving the village, there’s a lot of houses like this that are actually abandoned.
Upsound Fezeka: You need to sleep early so that you get up at night, most of these killings happen at night, We take turns in sleeping, we sleep in groups, Its crazy
V/O like many of the residents here Matshawule believes the villagers have been left at the mercy of this ruthless killer.
Upsound Fezeka Matshawule: We thought we don’t belong in South Africa, we felt that this village doesn’t belong because how can people die and nothing gets done
V/O: Following the 7th murder tensions grew in the community, it all came to a head. It is alleged that angry community members rounded up 7 young men they suspected were behind the attacks. 5 of the men were burnt to death and the other two we hanged in a forest nearby.
V/O But the bodies still kept piling, bringing the number of people killed to 11 in just 8 months
-Timeline- graphics - Last 4 murders
Masa question: 15:30 After those young men were killed the murders continued, how did the community feel?
Upsound Fezeka: It’s actually not anger anymore it’s sadness, because you cant, have your grandmother and grandfather murdered and nothing gets done.
V/O : SAPS provincial spokesperson for the Eastern Cape Brigadier Thembinkosi Kinana says they are making inroads.
Upsound Brig Kinana: We decided as the management to the SAPS to set up a multidisciplinary team to prioritize every one of those cases. All these units must come together, the forensics, the crime intelligence, and many other units within the SAPS to make sure our investigation leaves no stone unturned.
Masa question: From your investigation, do you suspect a serial killer because the MO is
Similar?
UpsoundBrigadier Kinana: We can’t say with certainty that there is a serial killer at this stage however we are continuing with our investigation.
Masa: Like I say I’ve spent time with the community, they are not feeling the engagement from SAPS side.I want to go to the clues, there was a jacket and gloves given to the SAPS. what do we know about this piece of evidence?

Upsound Brig Kinana: from day one we were there in that community, our top management in the province, we even went to the extent that we strengthen the structures of the community policing forum, with the very same community.
Masa : I’ve been there for the past few days, I haven’t seen any of your members there.
Up sound Brig Kinana: We have our intelligence there, so if you talk for instance about our intelligence, you are not going to see them because they are working among the people, they are part of the community, they form a network.
Masa: Brigadier, an array of units involved, you are saying no stone unturned, but the deaths and killings keep happening, we are sitting at 11 with no arrests.Its unacceptable Brigadierr.
Up sound Brig Kinana: Of course, any single death is one too many, it’s unacceptable, even the structures of the SAPS visited each and every family there, with groceries, giving support…
Masa: Brigadier they don’t want visits from politicians, they want arrests.
Upsound Brig Kinana: I am not trying to mystify the issue of the work of the police, but remember we are also a professional, transformed police service.
Masa : I want to go to the clues that you talk about, there was a jacket and glove given to the SAPS, what do we know about this piece of evidence?
Upsound Brig KInana : Whatever it is that we collected was sent to the forensic lab, we are still waiting for the results, some of the results came and they came negative, some are still awaited/
V/O With every day that passes without the killer being caught this community grows desperate and as darkness falls tonight the people of Zngzingolweni are left not knowing if they will see another day.

Visual of house lights switching off-


end

Promos: Zingqolweni in the Eastern Cape has come to be known as the village of death, where 11 people were viciously killed in just a few months by a suspected serial killer. We visit this community living in constant fear [ Upsound] - 21 seconds
Promos: 11 elderly people were killed in a small village in the Eastern Cape in just 8 Months, we search for answers as the community of Zigqolweni fears a serial killer might be on the loose. - 11 seconds
Promos: Zigqolweni village in the Eastern Cape is under siege, 11 elderly people have been brutally killed in just 8 months we visit this community living on the edge.[ Upsound] - 21 secons

- The police are positive that they are making progress

metadata.Unique Selling Point: We still tend to think of small towns as a more innocent place, How could a murderer flourish in a place where everyone knows you by name, but behind the comfortable façade of small-town South Africa have lurked some very disturbed individuals. Lady Frere or Cacadu in the Eastern Cape is one such rural town where 11 elderly people were brutally murdered in just 10 months … This is a town beset with fear and haplessness… As many the community expects the killer to strike at any given time. Zangqolweni The gruesome killings started in December Last year where 50 year old Gcobile Fihla was found dead close to his house, he had been stabbed several times on his upper body and his throat was slit… initially the community though this was an isolated incident, but shockingly in February $ elerly women were killed in one night … the method of killing was very similar to the first murder -with the victims being stabbed several times and their throats slit. Following the killing Spree the community went on a rampage after they found yet another body ( a partially decomposed body of an elderly woman who had been stabbed and had her throat cut. The community rounded up 7 young people in the community and 4 were burnt to death, while the others were lynched near a forest. But the killings didn’t stop; on May 3 elderly people were killed – all consistent with the murderers MO, 3 more would die in the following months with the latest being a 71-year-old man.
metadata.Further information: What we know so Far : • The Modus Operandi is consistent , victims were stabbed on the upper body several times and had their throats slit. • The murderer targeted elderly who lived alone, or were alone at the time…it would seem they are from the community or had been stalking them for a while. • According to the little info released by police,stab wounds and slit is consistent with a right handed person. • No one in the community has taken responsibility for the vigilante killings. • According to journalist Lulamile Feni, some of the victims were raped. • There hasn’t been a murder since July. Treatment visually : • More than anything the story needs to capture the currently state of Zangqolweni village, this a rural community gripped by fear,people are afraid to leave their houses at night, there is this sense of eeriness just blanketing this community, especially because the killer hasn’t been found. • Though the community formed vigilante groups, there is fear that the killer is actually one of their own, we need to capture that fear. • We may need to touch on rural safety in the story – this may fit into out interview with the SAPS ( if they do grant us one). They have been vocal .. so I don’t think we’ll have a problem. • We will need to do re-enactments to tell the story, this will make it striking. • I feel like we should have more of dark / True -crime feel to in – in a rural setting ( we will need a really good camera guy.
